items.title: Alton Towers Resort

image.alt: Riders with arms in the air on a roller coaster

items.text: Big coasters for teens, CBeebies Land for little ones, plus a water park and hotels.
items.scout: Thrill rides first while queues are short, CBeebies Land after lunch.

items.title: LEGOLAND Windsor Resort

image.alt: Yellow, red, blue and green toy building bricks

items.text: Built for ages roughly 2 to 12: driving schools, gentle coasters and MINILAND.
items.scout: Head to the far side of the park first and work back.

items.title: Thorpe Park Resort

image.alt: A roller coaster track against a blue sky

items.text: Fast, big rides aimed squarely at teens and thrill-seeking adults.
items.scout: The teen pick near London. Check height limits for younger siblings.

items.title: Chessington World of Adventures

image.alt: People riding a spinning fairground ride

items.text: Family rides and a zoo in one ticket. A strong mixed-age day.
items.scout: Plan your route around the animal talks.

items.title: Paultons Park & Peppa Pig World

image.alt: A happy family running together in a sunlit garden

items.text: Peppa Pig World for toddlers, and the Viking-themed Valgard land (2026) for older kids.
items.scout: Do Peppa Pig World in the afternoon when it’s quieter.

items.title: Blackpool Pleasure Beach

image.alt: A roller coaster at an amusement park

items.text: A classic seaside park with historic coasters, right by the beach.
items.scout: Pair it with free beach time to stretch the day.

items.title: Drayton Manor Resort

image.alt: People riding a spinning fairground ride

items.text: Thrill rides plus Thomas Land, a whole area themed on Thomas & Friends for little engine fans.
items.scout: Thomas Land is a toddler dream. Bigger kids can do the coasters.

items.title: Flamingo Land

image.alt: A roller coaster track against a blue sky

items.text: A theme park and zoo combined, with rides for every age.
items.scout: Rides and animals in one ticket makes it great value for mixed ages.

items.title: Walt Disney World Resort

image.alt: Cinderella Castle at Magic Kingdom, Walt Disney World, Orlando

items.text: Four theme parks and two water parks. A holiday, not a day out.
items.scout: Two parks done well beat four done in a rush.

items.title: Universal Orlando Resort

image.alt: A castle-style building lit up at night

items.text: Three theme parks including Epic Universe, with the Wizarding World of Harry Potter across all three.
items.scout: Get park-to-park tickets to ride the Hogwarts Express.

items.title: Disneyland Resort

image.alt: A fairy-tale castle lit up at night

items.text: The original Disneyland and Disney California Adventure, side by side.
items.scout: The parks are next door, so park hopping is easy here.

items.title: Cedar Point

image.alt: Riders with arms in the air on a roller coaster

items.text: A legendary coaster park on Lake Erie, famous with thrill-seekers.
items.scout: Coaster-mad teens will rate this one. Check height limits.

items.title: Disneyland Paris

image.alt: Sleeping Beauty Castle at Disneyland Paris

items.text: Disneyland Park and Disney Adventure World, home of World of Frozen since March 2026.
items.scout: Do two days, and hit World of Frozen early.

items.title: Efteling

image.alt: Fireworks over a fairy-tale castle at night

items.text: A fairy-tale park with an enchanted forest walk and coasters for older kids.
items.scout: The Fairytale Forest suits toddlers and grandparents alike.

items.title: Europa-Park

image.alt: A roller coaster at an amusement park

items.text: Germany’s biggest theme park, themed on European countries.
items.scout: Plan two days. It’s huge.

items.title: PortAventura World

image.alt: Water slides at a water park

items.text: Theme park, Ferrari Land and a water park near the Costa Dorada beaches.
items.scout: Perfect add-on to a beach holiday.

items.title: LEGOLAND Billund

image.alt: A close-up of colourful toy building bricks

items.text: The original LEGOLAND, near LEGO House.
items.scout: Combine with LEGO House to make the trip worthwhile.

items.title: Parc Astérix

image.alt: People riding a spinning fairground ride

items.text: Funny, very French park with strong coasters and family rides.
items.scout: A great second park on a Paris trip.

items.title: Tivoli Gardens

image.alt: A fairy-tale castle lit up at night

items.text: One of the world’s oldest amusement parks (1843), magical after dark.
items.scout: Go in the evening for the lights.

items.title: Phantasialand

image.alt: Riders with arms in the air on a roller coaster

items.text: Richly themed park famous for its intense coasters, with family areas too.
items.scout: A bucket-list park for coaster-loving teens.

items.title: Sandcastle Waterpark

image.alt: Water slides at a water park

items.text: A big indoor water park on Blackpool’s seafront: slides, wave pool and toddler areas.
items.scout: Indoor and warm, so it’s rain-proof. No longer on new Merlin passes.

items.title: Center Parcs
items.where: Forest villages across the UK and Ireland

image.alt: A family walking along a wooden boardwalk through a field at golden hour

items.text: Forest short breaks built around an indoor tropical pool, bikes and activities.
items.scout: A short break, not a day out. Midweek breaks are usually cheaper.

items.title: Rulantica

image.alt: Water slides at a water park

items.text: A huge Scandinavian-themed indoor water world beside Europa-Park.
items.scout: Give it its own day rather than squeezing it in.

items.title: Siam Park

image.alt: Water slides at a water park

items.text: A Thai-themed water park in Tenerife with famous slides and a giant wave pool.
items.scout: Arrive early and grab a sunbed. Suncream on!

items.title: Universal’s Volcano Bay

image.alt: Water slides at a water park

items.text: Universal Orlando’s volcano-themed water park with virtual queuing.
items.scout: A great rest day between theme parks.

items.title: Disney’s Typhoon Lagoon

image.alt: A family walking on the beach holding hands

items.text: Disney’s shipwreck-themed water park with a big surf pool and gentle areas for little ones.
items.scout: Check seasonal opening: Disney water parks close for refurbishment at times.

items.title: Your local leisure pool

image.alt: Water slides at a water park

items.text: Flumes, wave machines and inflatable sessions at local pools.
items.scout: Look for family swim sessions and fun inflatable times.

items.title: Chester Zoo

image.alt: Two giraffes standing side by side

items.text: One of the UK’s biggest zoos, run by a conservation charity.
items.scout: Comfy shoes! It’s a big site.

items.title: London Zoo

image.alt: A mother gorilla hugging her baby

items.text: The world’s oldest scientific zoo, run by ZSL.
items.scout: Check the National Rail Days Out Guide offer first.

items.title: Longleat

image.alt: A safari vehicle driving through dry bush

items.text: A drive-through safari park plus a stately home and adventure play.
items.scout: Windows up where the signs say: monkeys love car aerials.

items.title: West Midland Safari Park

image.alt: A cheetah standing on a rock

items.text: A drive-through safari plus walk-through areas and family rides.
items.scout: Do the drive-through first, then the walk-round areas.

items.title: Yorkshire Wildlife Park

image.alt: A boy feeding deer through a fence

items.text: Walk-through wildlife park known for its polar bears.
items.scout: Walkways are long but flat, which is good for buggies.

items.title: Edinburgh Zoo

image.alt: A visitor watching a penguin swim past the glass

items.text: A hillside zoo famous for its penguins.
items.scout: Hilly, so bring a sturdy buggy or carrier.

items.title: SEA LIFE aquariums

image.alt: A toddler touching the glass of an aquarium tank

items.text: Indoor aquariums with sharks, rays and penguins at some centres.
items.scout: Perfect rainy-day rescue, usually 1.5–2 hours.

items.title: San Diego Zoo

image.alt: Two giraffes standing side by side

items.text: World-famous zoo in Balboa Park.
items.scout: Use the bus tour to save little legs.

items.title: Monterey Bay Aquarium

image.alt: An adult and child looking into a large aquarium tank

items.text: Sea otters, kelp forests and a giant open-ocean tank.
items.scout: Don’t miss the otter feeds.

items.title: ZooParc de Beauval

image.alt: A cheetah standing on a rock

items.text: One of Europe’s best-known zoos, with giant pandas and a cable car.
items.scout: Two days lets you see it all.

items.title: Farm parks & petting farms

image.alt: A young boy feeding an animal at a farm park

items.text: Feeding lambs, tractor rides, play barns and bouncy pillows.
items.scout: Lambing season in spring is extra special.

items.title: Pick-your-own farms

image.alt: A girl carrying a pumpkin she has picked

items.text: Strawberries in summer, apples and pumpkins in autumn. Pay for what you pick.
items.scout: Go early in the season for the best pickings.

items.title: Pumpkin picking

image.alt: Two children sitting on a hay bale surrounded by pumpkins

items.text: Hay-bale mazes, wheelbarrows and the perfect carving pumpkin.
items.scout: Book a timed slot at weekends and wear wellies.

items.title: Natural History Museum

image.alt: The vaulted Hintze Hall at the Natural History Museum, London

items.text: Dinosaurs, a blue whale skeleton and an earthquake room. Free general admission.
items.scout: Arrive at opening for the dinosaur gallery.

items.title: Science Museum

image.alt: A museum hall with a whale skeleton hanging from the ceiling

items.text: Space, flight and hands-on science. Free general admission.
items.scout: Some interactive galleries charge. Check before you go.

items.title: Young V&A

image.alt: A close-up of colourful toy building bricks

items.text: A free museum designed for children and young people, full of play and design.
items.scout: Brilliant for under-10s on a wet day.

items.title: National Museum of Scotland

image.alt: Looking up at a dinosaur skeleton in a museum

items.text: Dinosaurs, Dolly the sheep and hands-on galleries. Free general admission.
items.scout: Head up to the rooftop terrace for city views.

items.title: Eureka! The National Children’s Museum

image.alt: A boy leaning on the glass of an aquarium full of fish

items.text: A hands-on museum made for children, with play-based galleries.
items.scout: Best for under-11s. Book ahead in the holidays.

items.title: National Space Centre

image.alt: Visitors exploring a dinosaur fossil gallery

items.text: Rockets, a planetarium and space galleries.
items.scout: Catch a planetarium show: check times on arrival.

items.title: Royal Observatory Greenwich

image.alt: Two adults and a child looking out at a mountain view

items.text: Stand on the Prime Meridian and catch a planetarium show.
items.scout: Greenwich Park next door is free and great for a picnic.

items.title: Smithsonian museums

image.alt: Visitors exploring a dinosaur fossil gallery

items.text: Most Smithsonian museums are free, including Natural History and Air and Space.
items.scout: Two museums a day max with younger kids.

items.title: Exploratorium

image.alt: A boy leaning on the glass of an aquarium full of fish

items.text: Hundreds of hands-on science exhibits on San Francisco’s waterfront.
items.scout: Teens love the evening events: check the age rules.

items.title: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex

image.alt: Two adults and a child looking out at a mountain view

items.text: Real rockets, astronaut stories and the Space Shuttle Atlantis.
items.scout: An easy add-on to an Orlando trip. Check launch schedules.

items.title: Cité des Sciences et de l’Industrie

image.alt: A museum hall with a whale skeleton hanging from the ceiling

items.text: One of Europe’s biggest science museums, with a dedicated children’s area.
items.scout: Book the children’s area (Cité des enfants) in advance.

items.title: NEMO Science Museum

image.alt: An adult and child looking into a large aquarium tank

items.text: A hands-on science museum in a striking green building, with a rooftop terrace.
items.scout: Great on a rainy Amsterdam day.

items.title: Your local museum

image.alt: Looking up at a dinosaur skeleton in a museum

items.text: Many local museums are free and run holiday trails and crafts.
items.scout: Ask at the desk for a kids’ trail sheet.

items.title: Warwick Castle

image.alt: A stone castle under white clouds

items.text: A medieval castle with shows, towers and family events.
items.scout: Climb the towers early, before queues build. It’s on the Merlin pass.

items.title: Alnwick Castle

image.alt: A grey stone castle against a blue sky

items.text: Hogwarts in the first two Harry Potter films. Try broomstick training.
items.scout: Broomstick training is pure joy for young wizards.

items.title: Tower of London

image.alt: A grey stone castle against a blue sky

items.text: The Crown Jewels, Yeoman Warders and nearly 1,000 years of history.
items.scout: Join a Yeoman Warder tour: they’re great storytellers.

items.title: Edinburgh Castle

image.alt: A stone castle under white clouds

items.text: Scotland’s famous castle, with the Honours of Scotland and city views.
items.scout: Book a timed ticket online. Popular slots go fast.

items.title: Dover Castle

image.alt: A grey stone castle against a blue sky

items.text: A huge medieval castle with secret wartime tunnels beneath.
items.scout: English Heritage members go free.

items.title: Caernarfon Castle

image.alt: A stone castle under white clouds

items.text: A mighty medieval fortress cared for by Cadw.
items.scout: Climb the towers for views over the Menai Strait.

items.title: Stonehenge

image.alt: A family walking together on a grassy hill

items.text: The world-famous stone circle, with a visitor centre and Neolithic houses.
items.scout: Book ahead. Members of English Heritage go free.

items.title: Neuschwanstein Castle

image.alt: Cinderella Castle reflected in the moat at Magic Kingdom

items.text: The fairy-tale castle on the hill in the Bavarian Alps.
items.scout: Tickets are timed. Book well ahead in summer.

items.title: Heritage Open Days

image.alt: A grey stone castle against a blue sky

items.text: Hundreds of historic places open for free, with tours and family events.
items.scout: Some events need booking. Check the website in August.

items.title: Lake District National Park

image.alt: A family walking together on a grassy hill

items.text: Lakes, fells and boat trips. Some of England’s best walking.
items.scout: Pick a short lakeside walk with a café at the end.

items.title: Peak District National Park

image.alt: A family walking through a field with their dog

items.text: Caves, edges and trails, easy to reach from many cities.
items.scout: Former railway trails are flat and great for bikes and buggies.

items.title: Giant’s Causeway

image.alt: Two parents and a child holding hands on the seashore

items.text: Thousands of hexagonal basalt columns, and a legend about a giant.
items.scout: Walking to the stones is free. The visitor centre charges.

items.title: Eden Project

image.alt: A happy family running together in a sunlit garden

items.text: Giant biomes with a rainforest inside, plus play areas and events.
items.scout: The rainforest biome is warm. Wear layers.

items.title: Kew Gardens

image.alt: A family relaxing on a picnic blanket in a park

items.text: World-famous gardens with a treetop walkway and children’s play garden.
items.scout: The treetop walkway is a hit with all ages.

items.title: Yosemite National Park

image.alt: Deer grazing in a meadow below Half Dome in Yosemite

items.text: Waterfalls, giant sequoias and granite cliffs.
items.scout: Check if timed-entry reservations apply in peak season.

items.title: Grand Canyon National Park

image.alt: Two adults and a child looking out at a mountain view

items.text: One of the world’s great views, with easy rim walks.
items.scout: Stick to rim trails with young kids. Carry water.

items.title: Yellowstone National Park

image.alt: Deer grazing in a meadow below Half Dome in Yosemite

items.text: Geysers, hot springs and bison, in the world’s first national park.
items.scout: Stay on boardwalks in thermal areas: it’s dangerous off them.

items.title: Country parks & forests

image.alt: A child in yellow wellies walking through autumn leaves

items.text: Trails, play areas, bug hunts and den building, all free (parking may charge).
items.scout: Pack a picnic and make it a full day.

items.title: Geocaching treasure hunts

image.alt: A boy and girl walking across a green field

items.text: Use a free app to find hidden “caches” near you: a real-world treasure hunt.
items.scout: Brilliant for turning a walk into a mission.

items.title: Stargazing at a dark sky place

image.alt: A fairy-tale castle lit up at night

items.text: Dark sky parks and reserves have some of the best night skies around.
items.scout: Go on a moonless night and let eyes adjust for 20 minutes.

items.title: Rock pooling

image.alt: Two parents and a child holding hands on the seashore

items.text: Crabs, anemones and starfish. Free fun at low tide.
items.scout: Check tide times, and always put creatures back gently.

items.title: Jurassic Coast fossil hunting

image.alt: A family walking on the beach holding hands

items.text: A World Heritage coastline famous for fossils on its beaches.
items.scout: Search the beach, not the cliffs, and check tide times.

items.title: A classic seaside day

image.alt: A family walking on the beach holding hands

items.text: Sandcastles, pier arcades, crazy golf and chips on the prom.
items.scout: Choose lifeguarded beaches and swim between the red and yellow flags.

items.title: Go Ape treetop adventures

image.alt: Riding a zip line through a forest

items.text: Rope bridges, zip wires and Tarzan swings high in the trees.
items.scout: Check the age and height rules for each course before booking.

items.title: Zip World

image.alt: Sliding along a zip line

items.text: Big zip lines, underground adventures and trampolines in caverns.
items.scout: Weight and age limits apply to some rides. Check first.

items.title: iFLY indoor skydiving
items.where: Centres in the UK and worldwide

image.alt: Hot air balloons rising over the landscape

items.text: Float on a column of air in a vertical wind tunnel. No plane needed.
items.scout: Check minimum ages and weight limits for your centre.

items.title: High ropes & climbing towers

image.alt: Riding a zip line through a forest

items.text: Many activity centres and farm parks have low and high ropes courses.
items.scout: Low ropes courses suit younger kids. Start there.

items.title: Trampoline parks

image.alt: An indoor trampoline park

items.text: Wall-to-wall trampolines, foam pits and dodgeball courts.
items.scout: Look for toddler-only sessions for under-5s. Grip socks needed.

items.title: Bowling

image.alt: A bowling ball hitting the pins

items.text: Bumpers for little ones and fierce family rivalries for teens.
items.scout: Weekday daytime games are often cheaper.

items.title: Laser tag

image.alt: A neon sign for escape rooms

items.text: Team games in a neon arena. Brilliant for birthdays.
items.scout: Check minimum ages: some arenas are 7+.

items.title: Soft play

image.alt: An indoor obstacle course with a foam pit

items.text: Slides, ball pits and climbing frames built for little ones.
items.scout: Term-time weekday mornings are calmest.

items.title: Kids’ cinema mornings

image.alt: A neon sign for escape rooms

items.text: Many cinema chains run cheaper kids’ screenings in the holidays.
items.scout: Check your local cinema’s holiday kids’ club.

items.title: Arcades & games centres
items.where: Seafronts and leisure parks near you

image.alt: A neon sign for escape rooms

items.text: Retro machines, air hockey and VR games.
items.scout: Set a budget on a play card before you start.

items.title: Climbing & bouldering walls

image.alt: Climbing an indoor bouldering wall

items.text: Taster sessions teach the basics. Bouldering needs no ropes.
items.scout: Book a family taster first: staff set you up safely.

items.title: Escape rooms

image.alt: A neon sign for escape rooms

items.text: Solve puzzles as a team to “escape” in 60 minutes.
items.scout: Ask for a family or beginner room, and the minimum age.

items.title: Self-guided treasure trails

image.alt: A boy and girl walking across a green field

items.text: Follow clues around a town to solve a mystery, at your own pace.
items.scout: Great for making a town walk feel like an adventure.

items.title: Go-karting

image.alt: Two go-kart drivers on a race track

items.text: Junior and family sessions at indoor and outdoor tracks.
items.scout: Age and height rules vary by track. Check before booking.

items.title: Skate parks

image.alt: A skateboarder at a skate park at sunset

items.text: Free ramps for scooters, skateboards and BMX.
items.scout: Helmets on, and go early before it gets busy.

items.title: Roller skating rinks

image.alt: Skate park ramps covered in graffiti

items.text: Disco lights, music and roller skates. A retro favourite.
items.scout: Beginners’ sessions are less hectic.

items.title: Traffic-free family bike rides
items.where: Trails and cycle paths near you

image.alt: A family walking through a field with their dog

items.text: Old railway paths and forest trails: flat, car-free and great with bike hire.
items.scout: Choose a route with a café or playground halfway.

items.title: Surf lessons in Cornwall & Devon
items.where: North Cornwall and North Devon beaches

image.alt: A group of people learning to surf

items.text: Beginner surf lessons with wetsuit and board included at many surf schools.
items.scout: Pick a school with qualified instructors and lifeguarded beaches.

items.title: The Wave

image.alt: A surfer riding a wave on an orange board

items.text: An inland surf lake with waves on demand, and lessons for beginners.
items.scout: Check minimum ages for lessons before booking.

items.title: Kayaking & paddleboarding
items.where: Lakes, rivers and coasts near you

image.alt: A group of people learning to surf

items.text: Guided taster sessions on calm water are a great first go.
items.scout: Always wear a buoyancy aid, and go with a guide first.

items.title: The Snowdome

image.alt: People skating on an outdoor ice rink

items.text: Real indoor snow for ski and snowboard lessons, sledging and ice skating.
items.scout: Beginner lessons are the best way in. Gloves are a must.

items.title: Chill Factore

image.alt: People skating on an outdoor ice rink

items.text: An indoor real-snow slope with lessons and snow play.
items.scout: Snow play sessions suit younger kids who aren’t ready to ski.

items.title: Ice skating rinks
items.where: Ice rinks near you (plus winter pop-ups)

image.alt: Skating on an ice rink

items.text: Year-round rinks and festive outdoor rinks in winter.
items.scout: Skate aids help little ones find their feet.

items.title: Hyde Park Winter Wonderland

image.alt: Twinkling red and white festive lights

items.text: A huge seasonal festival with rides, an ice rink, markets and shows.
items.scout: Weekday daytime visits are calmer. Some attractions are ticketed separately.

items.title: The Jacobite steam train

image.alt: A steam train crossing the Glenfinnan Viaduct in the Scottish Highlands

items.text: The “Hogwarts Express” route over the Glenfinnan Viaduct. Seasonal.
items.scout: No tickets? Watching it cross the viaduct is free.

items.title: Heritage steam railways

image.alt: A heritage steam train passing through a forest

items.text: Short rides behind real steam engines, plus themed event days.
items.scout: Check the timetable. Most don’t run every day.

items.title: Santa experiences
items.where: Farms, gardens and railways near you (December)

image.alt: A family gathered around a Christmas tree

items.text: Grottos, elves, crafts and a gift from the big man himself.
items.scout: Book in October for the best slots.

items.title: Christmas light trails

image.alt: Twinkling red and white festive lights

items.text: Illuminated evening trails through gardens and parks.
items.scout: Early-evening weekday slots are often cheaper.

items.title: Warner Bros. Studio Tour London

image.alt: A Platform 9¾ sign for the Hogwarts Express

items.text: Real Harry Potter sets, props and costumes. Under-5s free.
items.scout: Allow 3–4 hours and book direct.

items.title: Platform 9¾ at King’s Cross

image.alt: A red steam locomotive on a railway line

items.text: The trolley vanishing into the wall. Your own photo is free.
items.scout: Go early to beat the queue.

items.title: Warner Bros. Studio Tour Tokyo

image.alt: A castle-style building lit up at night

items.text: The Making of Harry Potter, in Tokyo since 2023.
items.scout: Book timed tickets well ahead.

items.title: Universal Studios Hollywood

image.alt: Riders with arms in the air on a roller coaster

items.text: A working film studio with a famous Studio Tour, rides and a Wizarding World.
items.scout: Do the Studio Tour early, before queues build.
